hero.headline: 86-year-old woman dies after crash at Port St. Lucie intersection
hero.body:
An 86-year-old woman died Thursday after failing to yield at a Port St. Lucie intersection and being struck by an SUV driven by a 17-year-old boy. Marie R. Martin was driving a 2006 Hyundai Elantra west on Southwest Lawndale Avenue when she entered the intersection with Southwest Savona Boulevard from near a stop sign and failed to yield to a northbound 2026 Honda HR-V at approximately 2:30 p.m.

The Honda struck the driver's side of Martin's Hyundai in a T-bone collision. The impact left the Hyundai off the roadway near a cluster of palm trees with visible damage to its driver's side. The Honda came to rest on the grass nearby, close to vegetation and a roadside sign. Debris and emergency equipment were scattered across the grass between the two vehicles.

St. Lucie Fire Rescue extricated Martin from the Hyundai before transporting her to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with critical injuries. She later died at the hospital despite efforts to save her. The 17-year-old driver of the Honda was not injured in the crash.

The Port St. Lucie Police Department's Traffic Homicide Unit continues to investigate the crash at the intersection east of Interstate 95. Body-camera video recorded after the crash shows Port St. Lucie police officers and St. Lucie County Fire District personnel at the scene, along with fire engines, rescue vehicles and traffic cones blocking part of the intersection.

A 2006 Hyundai Elantra, driven by Marie R. Martin, was traveling westbound near the stop sign on Southwest Lawndale Avenue. Investigators determined that Martin entered the intersection and failed to yield the right-of-way to the northbound Honda, resulting in the Honda striking the driver's side of the Hyundai. This caused the Honda to T-bone the Hyundai. Martin was extricated by St. Lucie Fire Rescue and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with critical injuries. Martin later succumbed to her injuries. The 17-year-old driver was not injured in the crash. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

cards.headline: Man accused of attacking convicted killer Otto Lenke in St. Lucie County Jail
cards.teaser: Robert Castro allegedly struck convicted murderer Otto Lenke in the face inside a jail dorm on July 6, knocking off his glasses and cutting his nose.
cards.body:
Robert Castro struck Otto Lenke in the face inside a St. Lucie County Jail dorm on July 6, knocking off his glasses and cutting the upper part of his nose, according to an arrest affidavit. A jail sergeant witnessed Castro strike Lenke, and surveillance video showed Castro approaching Lenke and hitting him in the face. Lenke told a detective he had been using a jail-issued tablet to watch a chess game when Castro attacked him.

Castro, 30, is charged with battery by a person detained in a prison or jail facility, a felony. The charge was filed July 20. When investigators attempted to interview Castro on July 16, he repeatedly stated that he did not understand his Miranda rights and did not want to speak with the detective, ending the interview.

Lenke, a former Melbourne police officer and Indian River County firefighter, was convicted in May of first-degree murder and first-degree arson in the 2021 death of Richard Benson. Castro was convicted in 2024 of first-degree murder with a firearm in the death of his former girlfriend, Taylor Ann Sato, but the Fourth District Court of Appeal reversed the conviction in February after finding that the trial court failed to properly complete the process for determining whether Castro was competent to stand trial.
cards.article_text: A man awaiting a possible retrial in the fatal shooting of his former girlfriend is accused of attacking convicted murderer Otto Lenke inside the St. According to an arrest affidavit, Robert Castro approached Lenke in a jail dorm on July 6 and struck him in the face, knocking off his glasses. Lenke approached an intercom and reported the attack to corrections staff, the affidavit says. A deputy noticed a cut on the upper part of Lenke’s nose, and a nurse treated the injury. A jail sergeant witnessed Castro strike Lenke, according to investigators. Surveillance video also showed Castro approaching Lenke and hitting him in the face, the affidavit says. Lenke later told a detective he had been using a jail-issued tablet to watch a chess game when Castro attacked him. Investigators attempted to interview Castro on July 16. The affidavit says Castro repeatedly stated that he did not understand his Miranda rights and did not want to speak with the detective, ending the interview. Castro, 30, is charged with battery by a person detained in a prison or jail facility, a felony. The new charge was filed July 20. Lenke, a former Melbourne police officer and Indian River County firefighter, was convicted in May of first-degree murder and first-degree arson in the 2021 death of Richard Benson. Prosecutors said Lenke shot Benson three times inside Benson’s Fort Pierce motorcycle shop, poured an accelerant on him and set him on fire while he was still alive. A jury later voted 11-1 to recommend that Lenke be sentenced to death. Castro’s murder conviction reversed Castro was convicted in 2024 of first-degree murder with a firearm in the death of his former girlfriend, Taylor Ann Sato, and sentenced to life in prison. However, the Fourth District Court of Appeal reversed the conviction in February after finding that the trial court failed to properly complete the process for determining whether Castro was competent to stand trial. A psychologist found Castro competent in November 2022. Five days later, his attorneys raised concerns about his condition, and the original judge said Castro had definitely decompensated before ordering another evaluation. The appeals court said the record contained no additional evaluation, report or competency hearing after that order. Nearly two years later, a different judge declared Castro competent based on the original 2022 evaluation. Castro then went to trial and was convicted. The appellate court ruled that a two-year-old evaluation was not sufficient because competency must be assessed close to the time of trial. The case was sent back to the trial court to determine whether Castro’s competency during the 2024 trial can now be reliably evaluated. Castro would receive a new trial if a retrospective evaluation cannot be conducted or if the court determines he was not competent during the original trial. 2022 killing Fort Pierce police accused Castro of killing Sato outside her Timber Ridge Lane home during the early morning hours of July 23, 2022. According to the original arrest affidavit, a man called 911 and said he had shot and killed his girlfriend and was considering killing himself. Officers arrived and found Sato outside the home with multiple gunshot wounds. Investigators reported finding six gunshot wounds and several 9 mm shell casings near her body. Sato’s stepfather told detectives that she and Castro had recently ended a long-term relationship. He said Sato had blocked Castro’s phone number, but Castro continued trying to contact her by sending repeated $1 transactions through Cash App with messages attached. The stepfather also told police Castro had previously threatened to kill Sato. After listening to part of the 911 call, he identified the caller’s voice as Castro’s, according to the affidavit. Castro later surrendered to deputies in St. Investigators said several rounds of 9 mm ammunition were found in his pocket. His police interview ended after an attorney arrived and directed detectives not to question him further.

Lenke approached an intercom and reported the attack to corrections staff, the affidavit says. A deputy noticed a cut on the upper part of Lenke’s nose, and a nurse treated the injury. A jail sergeant witnessed Castro strike Lenke, according to investigators. Surveillance video also showed Castro approaching Lenke and hitting him in the face, the affidavit says. Lenke later told a detective he had been using a jail-issued tablet to watch a chess game when Castro attacked him. Investigators attempted to interview Castro on July 16. The affidavit says Castro repeatedly stated that he did not understand his Miranda rights and did not want to speak with the detective, ending the interview. Castro, 30, is charged with battery by a person detained in a prison or jail facility, a felony. The new charge was filed July 20. Lenke, a former Melbourne police officer and Indian River County firefighter, was convicted in May of first-degree murder and first-degree arson in the 2021 death of Richard Benson. Prosecutors said Lenke shot Benson three times inside Benson’s Fort Pierce motorcycle shop, poured an accelerant on him and set him on fire while he was still alive. A jury later voted 11-1 to recommend that Lenke be sentenced to death. Castro’s murder conviction reversed Castro was convicted in 2024 of first-degree murder with a firearm in the death of his former girlfriend, Taylor Ann Sato, and sentenced to life in prison. However, the Fourth District Court of Appeal reversed the conviction in February after finding that the trial court failed to properly complete the process for determining whether Castro was competent to stand trial. A psychologist found Castro competent in November 2022. Five days later, his attorneys raised concerns about his condition, and the original judge said Castro had definitely decompensated before ordering another evaluation. The appeals court said the record contained no additional evaluation, report or competency hearing after that order. Nearly two years later, a different judge declared Castro competent based on the original 2022 evaluation. Castro then went to trial and was convicted. The appellate court ruled that a two-year-old evaluation was not sufficient because competency must be assessed close to the time of trial. The case was sent back to the trial court to determine whether Castro’s competency during the 2024 trial can now be reliably evaluated. Castro would receive a new trial if a retrospective evaluation cannot be conducted or if the court determines he was not competent during the original trial. 2022 killing Fort Pierce police accused Castro of killing Sato outside her Timber Ridge Lane home during the early morning hours of July 23, 2022. According to the original arrest affidavit, a man called 911 and said he had shot and killed his girlfriend and was considering killing himself. Officers arrived and found Sato outside the home with multiple gunshot wounds. Investigators reported finding six gunshot wounds and several 9 mm shell casings near her body. Sato’s stepfather told detectives that she and Castro had recently ended a long-term relationship. He said Sato had blocked Castro’s phone number, but Castro continued trying to contact her by sending repeated $1 transactions through Cash App with messages attached. The stepfather also told police Castro had previously threatened to kill Sato. After listening to part of the 911 call, he identified the caller’s voice as Castro’s, according to the affidavit. Castro later surrendered to deputies in St. Investigators said several rounds of 9 mm ammunition were found in his pocket. His police interview ended after an attorney arrived and directed detectives not to question him further.

cards.headline: Federal prosecutors say Guerrero's fentanyl sale was captured on doorbell camera in Indian River County
cards.teaser: The May 16, 2023 drug transaction between Alfonso Guerrero and David Eller was recorded on a doorbell camera at Eller's Vero Beach home.
cards.body:
Guerrero sold fentanyl in Indian River County on May 16, 2023, exchanging 0.1 gram of fentanyl for another controlled substance known as molly. The drug transaction was captured on a doorbell camera. Hours later, David Eller was found dead inside his Vero Beach home.

Investigators recovered drug paraphernalia, including a small piece of burnt aluminum foil that Eller used to receive the fentanyl from Guerrero on the victim's front porch, near his body. U.S. Attorney Markenzy Lapointe for the Southern District of Florida said a tenth of a gram of fentanyl, about the size of a small pinch of salt, was enough to kill Eller.

"This was not a small drug deal. Guerrero sold the fentanyl that killed his friend and, just two days later, was caught carrying more fentanyl for distribution. Today’s life sentence is the consequence of that deadly conduct and his long record of violence and crime. hero.headline: 86-year-old woman dies after Port St. Lucie intersection crash
hero.body:
Marie R. Martin, 86, died Thursday after her Hyundai Elantra was struck at the intersection of Southwest Savona Boulevard and Southwest Lawndale Avenue in Port St. Lucie. Port St. Lucie Police Department officers responded to the crash at approximately 2:30 p.m.

The preliminary investigation indicates Martin was driving a 2006 Hyundai Elantra westbound on Southwest Lawndale Avenue when she entered the intersection from near a stop sign and failed to yield the right of way to a northbound 2026 Honda HR-V driven by a 17-year-old boy. The Honda struck the driver's side of the Hyundai, causing the Honda to T-bone Martin's vehicle.

St. Lucie Fire Rescue extricated Martin from the Hyundai before transporting her to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with critical injuries. She later died at the hospital. Body camera video recorded after the crash shows the Hyundai off the roadway near a cluster of palm trees with visible damage to its driver's side and emergency crews working around the vehicle. The Honda came to rest on the grass nearby, close to vegetation and a roadside sign.

The 17-year-old driver of the Honda was not injured in the crash. The Port St. Lucie Police Department Traffic Homicide Unit continues to investigate the crash. The intersection is located east of Interstate 95.

The preliminary investigation indicates that a 2026 Honda HR-V, driven by a 17-year-old boy, was traveling northbound on Southwest Savona Boulevard approaching the intersection with SW Lawndale Avenue. A 2006 Hyundai Elantra, driven by Marie R. Martin, was traveling westbound near the stop sign on Southwest Lawndale Avenue. Investigators determined that Martin entered the intersection and failed to yield the right-of-way to the northbound Honda, resulting in the Honda striking the driver's side of the Hyundai. This caused the Honda to T-bone the Hyundai. Martin was extricated by St. Lucie Fire Rescue and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with critical injuries. Martin later succumbed to her injuries. The 17-year-old driver was not injured in the crash. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

cards.headline: King's Landing development in Fort Pierce nears completion of first luxury villas
cards.teaser: Construction is advancing on the King's Landing development project in downtown Fort Pierce, with nearly two residences sold and multiple villas nearing completion.
cards.body:
The King's Landing development project in downtown Fort Pierce is advancing with construction milestones. Brooke Harris, Team Lead of the Beachfront Brooke Team powered by Keller Williams Realty, said they are almost done with Villas 9 and 10, and the foundation has been laid for Villas 7 and 8. Two residences have been sold and are nearing completion.

The project features ten luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage, and a Marriott Hotel, which has signed an agreement for the development. The project is located in the waterfront district near the city marina and historic downtown. Harris said the location gives residents a walkability factor to go down to shopping, restaurants, retail, and the marina for boat storage.

Michelle Chaffee Cavalcanti, executive director of Main Street Fort Pierce, said the development has the potential to have a lot of impact on local businesses by bringing in visitors and giving local families somewhere for family members to stay when they visit. Officials said the estimated completion date is November 2029.
cards.article_text: The King's Landing development project in downtown Fort Pierce is advancing, with construction milestones bringing excitement to the community and local business owners. Brooke Harris, Team Lead of the Beachfront Brooke Team powered by Keller Williams Realty, shared updates on the progress. "They're almost done with Villa's 9 and 10, and then the foundation has already been in for 7 and 8," Harris said. She added that two residences have been sold and are nearing completion. The project features ten luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage, and a hotel. "We'll have the Marriott Hotel, which they have signed an agreement with, so that's great," Harris said. Officials emphasized the project's location in the waterfront district near the city marina and historic downtown. "It's waterfront, and it's connecting downtown to Edgartown, so it gives you that walkability factor to go down to shopping, restaurants, retail, and also, if you have a boat, you can store it right here at the marina," Harris said. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates Michelle Chaffee Cavalcanti, executive director of Main Street Fort Pierce, highlighted the significance of the development for the city. It's got the potential to have a lot of impact on our businesses, bringing in visitors, having our locals have somewhere for our families to stay when they come. But also, just being a destination where people can come walk, shop, live, and play," Chaffee Cavalcanti said. Business owners are optimistic about the benefits of having more residents in the downtown area, especially with most amenities within walking distance. "Well, it makes a huge impact because if you can just walk everywhere, it means that you can not only just walk to a restaurant, but you can walk into another business afterwards and shop and get information," Chaffee Cavalcanti said. She added, "It becomes an experience and not just a singular destination." Officials said the estimated completion date is November 2029. cards.headline: Port St. Lucie officer resigns after allegations he left scene where man later died by suicide
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie police officer resigned in April following allegations he failed to report a car at a church where a man was later found dead.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie police officer resigned in April following allegations of neglect during a March incident at the Treasure Coast Church of God Worship Center on Savona Boulevard, according to an internal affairs report. The report alleged Officer Mathew Brown came across a car with a man inside, looked, and then immediately left the scene.

Fifteen minutes later, another officer spotted the same car and discovered the man inside had died by suicide. Officer Brown arrived as backup but allegedly did not inform anyone about his earlier encounter with the vehicle and later claimed he did not see anything.

hero.headline: King's Landing development in downtown Fort Pierce nears construction milestones
hero.teaser: The King's Landing project in downtown Fort Pierce is advancing with luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage, and a Marriott Hotel.
hero.body:
The King's Landing development project in downtown Fort Pierce is advancing, with construction milestones bringing excitement to the community and local business owners. Brooke Harris, Team Lead of the Beachfront Brooke Team powered by Keller Williams Realty, said two residences have been sold and are nearing completion. The project features ten luxury villas, condos, retail spaces, restaurants, a parking garage, and a hotel in the waterfront district near the city marina and historic downtown.

Michelle Chaffee Cavalcanti, executive director of Main Street Fort Pierce, highlighted the significance of the development for the city. The project has the potential to impact local businesses by bringing in visitors and giving families a place to stay when they visit. Business owners are optimistic about having more residents in the downtown area, especially with most amenities within walking distance.

Officials said the estimated completion date is November 2029. Harris said the Marriott Hotel has signed an agreement for the development, which will connect downtown to Edgartown and provide walkability to shopping, restaurants, and retail.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie officer resigns after allegedly leaving scene where man later died by suicide
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie police officer resigned in April following allegations he left the scene of a car at a church on Savona Boulevard where a man was later found dead.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie police officer resigned in April following allegations of neglect during a March incident at the Treasure Coast Church of God Worship Center on Savona Boulevard, according to an internal affairs report. The report alleged Officer Mathew Brown came across a car with a man inside, looked, and then immediately left the scene.

Fifteen minutes later, another officer spotted the same car and discovered the man inside had died by suicide. Officer Brown arrived as backup but allegedly did not inform anyone about his earlier encounter with the vehicle and later claimed he did not see anything.

hero.headline: Stuart man jailed after fleeing traffic stop, leading police chase into Martin County
hero.body:
David Allen Kingsley Jr., 31, was arrested July 28 after fleeing a Stuart Police officer during a traffic stop and leading law enforcement on a chase that ended in Martin County with assistance from the Martin County Sheriff's Office and Florida Highway Patrol. Kingsley remains in the Martin County Jail on a $40,000 bond.

A Stuart Police officer stopped Kingsley on an equipment violation the evening of July 28. After the officer discovered that Kingsley's driver's license was revoked, Kingsley took off. Kingsley led officers on a brief pursuit within the City of Stuart, striking another vehicle before continuing out of the city.

Kingsley continued driving recklessly into Martin County jurisdiction, where deputies with the Martin County Sheriff's Office and troopers with the Florida Highway Patrol assisted in the pursuit. The vehicle was ultimately stopped, and Kingsley surrendered without further incident.

Kingsley was charged with two counts of fleeing eluding law enforcement, one count of leaving the scene of a crash involving property damage, failure to obey an officer's order to stop, reckless driving, and driving while license suspended or revoked. He was in the Martin County Jail as of July 30 on those charges.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware named Florida State League Pitcher of the Week
hero.body:
St. Lucie Mets pitcher Conner Ware has been named the Florida State League Pitcher of the Week for the week of July 20-26, Minor League Baseball announced. Ware made two appearances at Clover Park against Fort Myers, one start on Tuesday and one relief outing on Sunday.

The southpaw pitched 7.0 scoreless innings across both games. He scattered three hits, walked two and struck out 12. The Mets won both games with Ware getting credit for the win on Sunday.

Ware, 22, was drafted by the Mets in the 15th round out of LSU in 2025. He made his pro debut with St. Lucie in April and has been with the team all season.

This is the first FSL Pitcher or Player of the Week award for the Mets this season.

hero.headline: Los Angeles man sentenced to life in prison for fentanyl sale that killed Vero Beach resident
hero.body:
A Los Angeles man received a life sentence in federal prison for selling fentanyl that killed a Vero Beach resident and then continuing to traffic the deadly drug two days later. U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon imposed the sentence on Alfonso Guerrero, 39, of Los Angeles, after a federal jury convicted him in May 2026 of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute fentanyl resulting in death and distribution of fentanyl resulting in death.

According to court records and evidence presented at trial, Guerrero sold fentanyl in Indian River County. On May 16, 2023, he exchanged 0.1 gram of fentanyl, commonly known as a point, for another controlled substance known as molly. The drug transaction was captured on a doorbell camera. Hours later, David Eller was found dead inside his Vero Beach home. Investigators recovered drug paraphernalia, including a small piece of burnt aluminum foil that Eller used to receive the fentanyl from Guerrero on the victim's front porch, near his body.

Two days later, on May 18, 2023, Guerrero was arrested and found in possession of additional quantities of fentanyl intended for distribution. Guerrero's extensive criminal history included documented gang membership and prior convictions for attempted robbery with a firearm in California, aggravated assault in Georgia, and cocaine and fentanyl possession offenses in Florida.

U.S. Attorney Markenzy Lapointe for the Southern District of Florida said a tenth of a gram of fentanyl, about the size of a small pinch of salt, was enough to kill Eller. Prosecutors emphasized that Guerrero sold the fentanyl that killed his friend and just two days later was caught carrying more fentanyl for distribution. The case involved the DEA and local law enforcement partners tracing the fatal dose back to the dealer.
